subfamily: Sidecar riff on pisco, the lemon replaced by white verjus (the grapes' own acid), stirred as the Codex does its verjus sours (p. 187)
judged_by_hand: shaken (sours) finished ranges, by hand: a Sidecar is a sour, LI has no stirred-sour style (STUDIO-RULES check 2: anything else is freeform). The water line is the stirring melt from balance.py's stirred formula (stirred style: 127.5 ml -> 35.8% -> 173.1 ml), not water added; balance.py's own nearest style for the result is shaken
version: v1 (Tomás, round 3; round 4 step 1: style moved to freeform with the stirred melt modelled, drink unchanged). Sidecar structure (Codex: spirit, orange liqueur, sour) with the lemon out and white verjus in (Codex p. 187: 'a fairly large proportion of verjus to create a bright acidic backbone, especially in stirred sour drinks'; grapes' acids are tartaric and malic, LI p. 61). Pisco's bite curbed with blanc vermouth (Codex p. 159). Stirred: 127.5 ml -> 35.8% dilution -> 173 ml; 15.9% / 6.26 g / 0.757%, in Arnold's sour finished ranges by hand (15-19.7 / 5.0-8.9 / 0.76-0.94; acid an edge on the floor). Verjus values unsourced (6 g, 2.5%): proven for verjus acid 2.5-3.1% and sugar 3-10 g; pisco 38-48% all in. Soft verjus (2.0%) fallback, Checks only: + 5 ml tartaric solution -> 0.846%.

ingredients.note: melt from stirring on ice (stirred formula, 35.8%); not added
